title: Bouillabaisse
subtitle: Provençal saffron fish stew with rouille
excerpt: The great fish stew of Marseille: a deeply fragrant broth of saffron, fennel, tomato, and orange zest, loaded with several varieties of fish and shellfish, served with toasted bread and the fiery, garlicky rouille that is as essential as the stew itself.

recipe.sourceNotes: Bouillabaisse originated in Marseille as a fisherman's stew made with the unsellable bony rockfish left over after the day's catch was sold. The name comes from the Provençal 'bolhabaissa' (boil-down), referring to the method of rapidly boiling the fish to emulsify the olive oil into the broth. The Marseille version is strictly defined and uses specific Mediterranean rockfish; a home version uses the best firm white fish and shellfish available. The defining aromatics are saffron, fennel, orange zest, and the Provençal herb mixture. Rouille, a saffron-scented garlic mayonnaise, is spread on croûtons floated in the soup. The soup and fish are traditionally served separately: broth first, then the fish on a side plate.

content.text: Use at least two types of fish: a firm white fish that holds its shape (monkfish, sea bass) and a flakier fish (cod, haddock). Add shellfish in the last few minutes; they overcook quickly. The saffron must be bloomed in warm water before adding or its flavour and colour will not fully develop in the finished broth.

Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy pot. Cook the onion and fennel for 10 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, tomato puree, thyme, and orange zest. Cook for 2 minutes. Add the wine, increase the heat, and reduce by half.
Add the tinned tomatoes, fish stock, saffron water, and bay. Bring to a boil and simmer for 20 minutes. Season.

Add the cod and prawns. Cook for 3 minutes. Add the mussels, cover, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the mussels have opened; discard any that remain closed. Serve immediately with toasted baguette and rouille.
